title: Sell Mineral Rights in Thompson, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Thompson, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Thompson in Susquehanna County? We buy dry-gas Marcellus interests directly and pay cash without pressure.
heroLead: Thompson sits far enough into rural Susquehanna County that a lot of families here still think of themselves as living on a farm first, even though the gas company's mailings have shown up in that mailbox for close to two decades now.
intro: Thompson is a small township in northern Susquehanna County, close to the New York border, in a rural part of the dry-gas Marcellus fairway that saw dense leasing activity starting in 2008. Cabot Oil & Gas, now Coterra, built one of its earliest and most concentrated development areas across this part of the county, and farm tracts around Thompson were among the first in the state to see modern horizontal drilling.

That early start means a lot of Thompson-area wells have over a decade of production history, giving us solid data to work from, but it also means a lot of original leases here carry deduction terms that families have never revisited.

sections.heading: One of the Earliest Development Areas in the Whole Play
paragraphs: Thompson Township was part of the first wave of Marcellus horizontal drilling in Pennsylvania, which means units here have a longer track record than almost anywhere else in the state. That extended history supports a well-grounded, defensible valuation rather than a guess.

sections.heading: Reviewing an Original 2008-Era Lease
paragraphs: If your family's lease dates to the very start of the boom, it's worth pulling it out and reading the post-production deduction language carefully. Under Kilmer v. Elexco, gathering and compression deductions permitted by lease language have generally been upheld, and early leases often allowed broader deductions than what became standard later.

faqs.question: Why did development start so early specifically in Thompson Township?
faqs.answer: Early operators identified strong dry-gas potential in this part of Susquehanna County and moved quickly to lease and drill, making it one of the first areas of concentrated horizontal Marcellus development in the state.

faqs.question: Is my well still producing after all these years?
faqs.answer: Many wells drilled during the earliest development phase continue producing today, though at reduced rates compared to their initial output. We check current production data for your specific unit.

faqs.question: Should I get a copy of my original 2008 lease before contacting you?
faqs.answer: It helps, but isn't required. We can often locate a recorded copy at the Susquehanna County recorder of deeds if you no longer have your own.

faqs.question: Does being near the New York border affect my Thompson-area minerals?
faqs.answer: No. Your interest is governed entirely by Pennsylvania law as long as your parcel sits within Pennsylvania, regardless of how close it is to the state line.
